sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin, and I'm Mark Ronson, and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰，我是马克·罗森，欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一个专注于设计之美及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs, in the era of vinyl, every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you,
sentences.zh: 即使在我还在夜店当DJ的黑胶唱片时代，每天晚上你都要带着300件你最珍视的宝贝去工作，

sentences.en: and you turned a DJ booth into this, like, living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 然后你会把一个DJ台变成这样一个充满活力的快闪博物馆，里面摆满了精美的50年历史的藏品。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听来自爱彼的《重构者》。

sentences.en: Hey, it's Michael.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是迈克尔。

sentences.en: A quick note about today's show.
sentences.zh: 关于今天节目的简短说明。

sentences.en: As you all know, we're a news show, and so much of what we do is pursue the answers to big and urgent questions.
sentences.zh: 如大家所知，我们是一个新闻节目，我们的很大一部分工作就是寻求那些重大且紧迫问题的答案。

sentences.en: What will be the impact of a giant piece of legislation?
sentences.zh: 一项庞大的立法会产生什么影响？

sentences.en: Or what are the implications of a verdict in a major trial?
sentences.zh: 或者一场重大审判的判决意味着什么？

sentences.en: Recently, two of our Times colleagues, audio producer Bianca Gaver and science writer Dennis Overby, embarked on an effort to explore some of the universe's biggest questions.
sentences.zh: 最近，我们的两位《泰晤士报》同事，音频制作人比安卡·盖弗和科学作家丹尼斯·奥弗比，着手探索宇宙中一些最大的问题。

sentences.en: But this time, the point wasn't to deliver concrete answers.
sentences.zh: 但这一次，重点并不是给出具体的答案。

sentences.en: Instead, it was to sit with the kinds of big, dreamy, existential questions that we don't have answers to.
sentences.zh: 相反，它是去体会那些我们找不到答案的宏大、梦幻般的生存问题。

sentences.en: Today, we share some of the conversations that Bianca and Dennis have been having.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们分享一些比安卡和丹尼斯一直在进行的对话。

sentences.en: It's Friday, August 19th.
sentences.zh: 今天是8月19日，星期五。

sentences.en: Hi, Dennis.
sentences.zh: 嗨，丹尼斯。

sentences.en: It's Bianca.
sentences.zh: 我是比安卡。

sentences.en: Yeah, how are you?
sentences.zh: 嗨，你好吗？

sentences.en: I'm good.
sentences.zh: 我很好。

sentences.en: How are you?
sentences.zh: 你呢？

sentences.en: I'm fine.
sentences.zh: 我很好。

sentences.en: So, I'm talking to you, officer, on my iPhone.
sentences.zh: 所以，警官，我在用我的iPhone跟你说话。

sentences.en: I'm through my earbuds.
sentences.zh: 我通过耳机听着。

sentences.en: Is that okay?
sentences.zh: 这样可以吗？

sentences.en: Is this?
sentences.zh: 这样行吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, it sounds great.
sentences.zh: 可以，听起来很棒。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 行。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: What are we doing?
sentences.zh: 我们在做什么？

sentences.en: Why don't you just start by introducing yourself?
sentences.zh: 你为什么不先做个自我介绍呢？

sentences.en: Can you say your name and what you do at the Times?
sentences.zh: 你能说一下你的名字以及你在《泰晤士报》做什么吗？

sentences.en: My name is Dennis Overby, and for some reason, I get away with calling myself the Cosmic Affairs Correspondent of the New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我叫丹尼斯·奥弗比，不知为什么，我居然能顶着《纽约时报》宇宙事务记者的头衔到处晃悠。

sentences.en: That's what it says on my business cards.
sentences.zh: 我的名片上就是这么写的。

sentences.en: So, the title is Cosmic Affairs Correspondent.
sentences.zh: 所以，头衔就是宇宙事务记者。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So, my beat I describe as physics, the universe, anything having to do with Einstein, and anything else that I decide fits into that rubric.
sentences.zh: 所以，我报道的领域可以说是物理学、宇宙、任何与爱因斯坦有关的事物，以及任何其他我认为符合这一范畴的事情。

sentences.en: So, I'm interested in how people relate to their position or their role in a universe that we don't understand and probably never will.
sentences.zh: 因此，我感兴趣的是人们如何看待自己在我们不理解也可能永远不会理解的宇宙中的位置或角色。

sentences.en: So, we walk around under little bubbles of certainty that are occasionally rudely shattered, like the sudden emergence of a pandemic or worse.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们生活在一个个充满确信的小泡泡里，而这些泡泡偶尔会被无情地击碎，比如突然爆发的大流行病或更糟糕的事情。

sentences.en: We sort of think we can run our lives.
sentences.zh: 我们觉得自己能掌控生活。

sentences.en: We really can't.
sentences.zh: 其实我们根本不能。

sentences.en: What do you mean?
sentences.zh: 你是什么意思？

sentences.en: Well, you know, the brute truth of this is that the universe doesn't care.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，这背后的残酷真相是宇宙根本不在乎。

sentences.en: I mean, the stars in the sky, they don't know about us.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，天上的星星根本不认识我们。

sentences.en: We'll never know whether anybody's living there or not, probably.
sentences.zh: 我们可能永远不会知道那里到底有没有人居住。

sentences.en: And eventually, in a billion years, there will be no life on Earth because the sun will warm up and boil away the oceans.
sentences.zh: 而且最终，在十亿年后，地球上将不会有生命，因为太阳会变热并把海洋蒸发掉。

sentences.en: The human race will be forgotten.
sentences.zh: 人类将被遗忘。

sentences.en: So, in the far, far fullness of time, nothing will remain.
sentences.zh: 所以，在遥远而完全的未来，什么都不会剩下。

sentences.en: Does being the cosmic affairs correspondent make you depressed?
sentences.zh: 身为宇宙事务记者会让你感到沮丧吗？

sentences.en: Make me depressed?
sentences.zh: 让我沮丧？

sentences.en: What you said just now is very grim.
sentences.zh: 你刚才说的话太残酷了。

sentences.en: Well, it doesn't...
sentences.zh: 嗯，它并不……

sentences.en: I'm not depressed right now.
sentences.zh: 我现在并不沮丧。

sentences.en: I guess, um...
sentences.zh: 我想，嗯……

sentences.en: I mean, maybe I've always been depressed.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，也许我一直都很沮丧。

sentences.en: I'm definitely, I'm kind of a pessimiSt.
sentences.zh: 我绝对，我算是个悲观主义者。

sentences.en: But it doesn't depress me to write about these things because it seems like something that has to be illuminated.
sentences.zh: 但写这些东西并没有让我沮丧，因为这似乎是必须被阐明的事情。

sentences.en: It's part of our heritage as humans to, like, understand our predicament.
sentences.zh: 理解我们的困境是我们身为人类的遗产的一部分。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Because you're aware that, like, the universe could collapse tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 因为你意识到，比如，宇宙明天就可能崩溃。

sentences.en: It could.
sentences.zh: 确实可能。

sentences.en: You know, anything could happen.
sentences.zh: 你知道，什么事都有可能发生。

sentences.en: You know, the stock market could collapse tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 你知道，股市明天可能会崩盘。

sentences.en: So, I don't know about you,
sentences.zh: 所以，我不知道你怎么样，

sentences.en: but I'm getting all these emails these days about investment opportunities and where Elon Musk is putting his money now or click here to find out and better get it on the ground floor.
sentences.zh: 但我这些天收到了所有这些关于投资机会的电子邮件，比如埃隆·马斯克现在把钱投在哪里，或者点击这里了解详情，最好从底层开始投资。

sentences.en: But which ground floor are you going to get in on?
sentences.zh: 但你要从哪一个底层开始投资呢？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Um...
I think you were going to talk about, like, what you write about.
sentences.zh: 我想你本来想谈谈，比如，你写的内容。

sentences.en: Oh, right.
sentences.zh: 哦，对。

sentences.en: Because, so, lately, especially during the last year, I've written a lot about black holes.
sentences.zh: 因为，所以，最近，特别是在过去的一年里，我写了很多关于黑洞的文章。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: Black holes are the cat videos of astronomy.
sentences.zh: 黑洞就是天文学界的猫咪视频。

sentences.en: People can't get enough of them.
sentences.zh: 人们对它们百看不厌。

sentences.en: They have this kind of elemental attraction to them, right?
sentences.zh: 他们对黑洞有一种基础的吸引力，对吧？

sentences.en: They're, they're doomed.
sentences.zh: 它们是，它们注定要毁灭。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: And I have a history with black holes because I've been writing about black holes for years.
sentences.zh: 我和黑洞颇有渊源，因为我写黑洞已经好多年了。

sentences.en: 40, 45 years, I think.
sentences.zh: 我想有40、45年了。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Because long ago, at the beginning of my journalism career, I got a job as an assistant typesetter at a magazine called Sky and Telescope,
sentences.zh: 因为很久以前，在我新闻生涯的开始，我在一本名为《天空与望远镜》的杂志找到了一份助理排版员的工作，

sentences.en: which was an astronomy magazine published in Cambridge.
sentences.zh: 那是一本在剑桥出版的天文学杂志。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: At the time, back in the 1970s, black holes were kind of a controversial concept.
sentences.zh: 当时，在20世纪70年代，黑洞在某种程度上还是一个颇具争议的概念。

sentences.en: A lot of people didn't believe in them.
sentences.zh: 很多人不相信它们的存在。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: So, I got them to send me to a conference in which Stephen Hawking was talking about black holes.
sentences.zh: 所以我让他们派我去参加一个会议，斯蒂芬·霍金在会上谈论了黑洞。

sentences.en: And I went to England and followed him around Cambridge for a while, much to his annoyance.
sentences.zh: 我去了英国，在剑桥到处跟着他，这让他非常恼火。

sentences.en: And he had a great sense of humor, and he was sort of a smart aleck.
sentences.zh: 他很有幽默感，有点像个滑头。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: I mean, I didn't know at the time that I would, I would eventually write his obituary.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，当时我并不知道我最终会，会写他的讣告。

sentences.en: So, I've been identified with this subject for a long time.
sentences.zh: 所以，我长期以来一直与这个主题联系在一起。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: You know, it, it pulled me in because it does raise all these issues of mortality.
sentences.zh: 你知道，它，它吸引了我，因为它确实引发了关于生死的所有这些问题。

sentences.en: And what actually, what is the world made of?
sentences.zh: 而且实际上，世界是由什么组成的？

sentences.en: What is matter made of?
sentences.zh: 物质是由什么组成的？

sentences.en: If you can go into a black hole, disappear, right?
sentences.zh: 如果你能进入一个黑洞，然后消失，对吧？

sentences.en: You can just fully disappear.
sentences.zh: 你就可以彻底消失。

sentences.en: So, was it ever really here to begin with?
sentences.zh: 那么它一开始真的存在过吗？

sentences.en: I mean, how, you know, raises all these questions that are interesting to, to think about and are kind of on the edge of science.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，怎么，你知道，这引发了所有这些有趣的问题，值得去思考，并且处于科学的边缘。

sentences.en: So, yeah, black holes.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，黑洞。

sentences.en: So, it seems like your job is very philosophical, and you were called an evangelist of cosmic ignorance.
sentences.zh: 所以，听起来你的工作非常哲学，你被称为宇宙无知的传道者。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: What does that mean?
sentences.zh: 那是什么意思？

sentences.en: I love that phrase.
sentences.zh: 我很喜欢这个短语。

sentences.en: Because I believe cosmic ignorance reminds us of who we are, that we don't really know much about this universe we're in.
sentences.zh: 因为我相信宇宙无知提醒了我们究竟是谁，提醒我们对我们身处的这个宇宙其实知之甚少。

sentences.en: And, the whole thing in science is like, if you can formulate a question, you can find an answer to it.
sentences.zh: 而且，科学的核心就在于，如果你能提出一个问题，你就能找到它的答案。

sentences.en: But, it's not clear that we even know the right questions yet.
sentences.zh: 但是，我们甚至是否知道正确的问题还不清楚。

sentences.en: That's the kind of thing you often get from deeper thinkers.
sentences.zh: 这就是你经常能从更有思想的人那里听到的那种说法。

sentences.en: And, I don't know, I guess I think it's refreshing that we are so ignorant in a kind of a, you have to be very smart to find out how ignorant you are.
sentences.zh: 而且，我不知道，我想我觉得我们如此无知是一件很清新脱俗的事，你必须非常聪明才能发现自己有多无知。

sentences.en: We're like teenagers kind of trying to imagine what it's like to be in love.
sentences.zh: 我们就像试图想象恋爱是什么感觉的青少年一样。

sentences.en: I just find it refreshing because, yeah, maybe because there's no boss man who knows all the answers.
sentences.zh: 我只是觉得这很爽，因为，是的，也许因为没有一个知道所有答案的老板。

sentences.en: Like, there's no father who knows beSt.
sentences.zh: 就像没有一个无所不知的父亲一样。

sentences.en: We're all equal in our ignorance.
sentences.zh: 我们在无知面前都是平等的。

sentences.en: So, can you read me some of the cosmic questions you came up with?
sentences.zh: 所以，你能给我读一些你想到的宇宙问题吗？

sentences.en: Okay, let's see.
sentences.zh: 好吧，让我想想。

sentences.en: What's a black hole and why do we care what happens inside?
sentences.zh: 什么是黑洞，为什么我们要在意里面发生了什么？

sentences.en: Is there other life in the universe?
sentences.zh: 宇宙中还有其他生命吗？

sentences.en: Can you say these a bit more slowly and with a sense of drama?
sentences.zh: 你能说得慢一点，带点戏剧性吗？

sentences.en: What's a black hole and why do we care what happens inside?
sentences.zh: 什么是黑洞，为什么我们要在意里面发生了什么？

sentences.en: Is there other life in the universe?
sentences.zh: 宇宙中还有其他生命吗？

sentences.en: How come we don't already know?
sentences.zh: 为什么我们现在还不知道？

sentences.en: If there's other life in the universe, how come we don't already know about it?
sentences.zh: 如果宇宙中还有其他生命，为什么我们现在还不知道？

sentences.en: What's the fate of the earth and the universe?
sentences.zh: 地球和宇宙的命运是什么？

sentences.en: Are there other universes?
sentences.zh: 还有其他宇宙吗？

sentences.en: Do we have free will?
sentences.zh: 我们有自由意志吗？

sentences.en: Is there free will in the matrix?
sentences.zh: 黑客帝国里有自由意志吗？

sentences.en: What does that mean?
sentences.zh: 那是什么意思？

sentences.en: That's something I've been thinking about.
sentences.zh: 这是我一直在思考的问题。

sentences.en: Are there any good movies about science?
sentences.zh: 有什么关于科学的好电影吗？

sentences.en: This is something scientists talk about.
sentences.zh: 这是科学家们谈论的话题。

sentences.en: How do we know if there's life on it?
sentences.zh: 我们怎么知道上面有没有生命？

sentences.en: Will we ever live on Mars?
sentences.zh: 我们有一天会住在火星上吗？

sentences.en: Why do we remember the past and not the future?
sentences.zh: 为什么我们记得过去而不是未来？

sentences.en: And then did God have any choice creating the universe?
sentences.zh: 然后上帝在创造宇宙时有别的选择吗？

sentences.en: That was Einstein's question.
sentences.zh: 那是爱因斯坦的问题。

sentences.en: It's funny.
sentences.zh: 太搞笑了。

sentences.en: I was expecting them to be very science-y, but they're kind of speculative and hypothetical and almost science fiction-y.
sentences.zh: 我本以为它们会非常科学，但它们有点像推测性的、假设性的，几乎像是科幻小说。

sentences.en: They are.
sentences.zh: 确实是。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: That's what makes them fun, I think.
sentences.zh: 我想这就是它们的乐趣所在。

sentences.en: I'm not sure that I want to live in the real world that deeply, you know?
sentences.zh: 我不太确定我是否想那么深地生活在现实世界中，你知道吗？

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: After the break, Bianca and Dennis turn to one of life's most mystifying questions, and they go searching for some answers.
sentences.zh: 休息过后，比安卡和丹尼斯将探讨生活中最神秘的问题之一，并寻找一些答案。

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我负责《纽约时报》每日简报DealBook的商业与政策报道。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市DealBook峰会的现场采访商界、政界和文化界的一些最具影响力的领袖，包括J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde,
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、

sentences.en: Zylran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 齐尔兰·蒙达尼以及许多其他人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以观看其中一些毫无防备、未经过滤的对话实况。

sentences.en: We're going to be live-streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at NYTimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 我们将在11月18日于NYTimes.com上直播部分精选采访，供任何人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅者，可以下载《纽约时报》App来观看并获得一个月的免费阅读权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望大家能收听。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: Okay, so the question is based on something that Stephen Hawking said in a talk I heard him give probably 20 or 30 years ago,
sentences.zh: 好的，这个问题是基于斯蒂芬·霍金大约二三十年前的一次演讲中的内容，

sentences.en: which is, why do we remember the past but not the future?
sentences.zh: 也就是，为什么我们能记住过去，却记不住未来？

sentences.en: I guess the point is that we really don't understand all these notions that we take for granted,
sentences.zh: 我想重点在于，我们其实并不真正理解那些被我们视为理所当然的概念，

sentences.en: like time or space, right?
sentences.zh: 比如时间和空间，对吧？

sentences.en: And mathematically, it's treated like a dimension.
sentences.zh: 在数学上，它被当作一个维度来处理。

sentences.en: We tag things with where they are and when they are.
sentences.zh: 我们会给事物打上它们在何地以及何时发生的时间戳。

sentences.en: But that's not the way we live.
sentences.zh: 但这不是我们的生活方式。

sentences.en: We don't have a choice when we come out of the subway, whether we're going to go forward or backward in time,
sentences.zh: 当我们走地铁口时，我们没得选，无法决定在时间上是向前还是向后走，

sentences.en: the way we have a choice of saying going north or south or east or weSt.
sentences.zh: 就像我们可以选择向北、向南、向东或向西一样。

sentences.en: Like in math, we have the choice to change the time variable, but you're saying in life, we don't?
sentences.zh: 就像在数学中，我们可以选择改变时间变量，但你的意思是，在生活中我们不能？

sentences.en: We don't.
sentences.zh: 我们不能。

sentences.en: No, we don't.
sentences.zh: 对，我们不能。

sentences.en: We're stuck.
sentences.zh: 我们被困住了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Humans have always had some sort of way of marking the passage of time.
sentences.zh: 人类总是有某种方式来标记时间的流逝。

sentences.en: Think of Stonehenge and then think of the great clock towers.
sentences.zh: 想想巨石阵，再想想那些巨大的钟楼。

sentences.en: Time became more sort of a mathematical part of physics with Galileo.
sentences.zh: 随着伽利略的出现，时间在某种程度上成了物理学中数学的一部分。

sentences.en: And then Newton embellished that.
sentences.zh: 然后牛顿对这一点进行了完善。

sentences.en: And Newton kind of created this idea of like the universe is this kind of stage with a clock.
sentences.zh: 牛顿创造了一种观点，即宇宙就像是一个带有钟表的舞台。

sentences.en: And we were in it.
sentences.zh: 而我们就在其中。

sentences.en: And the stage stayed the same.
sentences.zh: 舞台保持不变。

sentences.en: The clock stayed the same.
sentences.zh: 时钟保持不变。

sentences.en: We just went through our paces.
sentences.zh: 我们只是按部就班地生活。

sentences.en: That worked fine until Einstein came along and showed that, well, clocks would measure time differently depending on where they are or how fast they were moving.
sentences.zh: 这运转得很好，直到爱因斯坦出现，他表明，嗯，根据时钟所在的位置或它们的运动速度，时钟测量的时间是不同的。

sentences.en: And space didn't stay the same.
sentences.zh: 空间也没有保持不变。

sentences.en: Things shrank and they expanded.
sentences.zh: 物体会收缩，也会膨胀。

sentences.en: And that's relativity.
sentences.zh: 这就是相对论。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: That's his famous theory of relativity.
sentences.zh: 这就是他著名的相对论。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That time is much more malleable than we realized.
sentences.zh: 时间比我们意识到的要具有可塑得多。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So speaking of Einstein, can you tell that story of a friend of his whose husband died?
sentences.zh: 说到爱因斯坦，你能讲讲他的一位女性朋友的丈夫去世的故事吗？

sentences.en: And the condolence letter?
sentences.zh: 还有那封慰问信？

sentences.en: Oh, right.
sentences.zh: 哦，对。

sentences.en: Oh, this is a famous letter that he wrote.
sentences.zh: 哦，这是他写的一封著名的信。

sentences.en: I wish I had the quotation in front of me.
sentences.zh: 我希望我能把这段引文直接念出来。

sentences.en: Maybe it's in my book.
sentences.zh: 也许在我的书里有。

sentences.en: I don't know if I can find it.
sentences.zh: 我不知道能不能找到它。

sentences.en: Let's see.
sentences.zh: 让我想想。

sentences.en: What's the name of your book?
sentences.zh: 你的书叫什么名字？

sentences.en: Einstein and Love.
sentences.zh: 《爱因斯坦与爱》。

sentences.en: So, okay.
sentences.zh: 所以，好吧。

sentences.en: Einstein's best friend, Michaela Besso, died in 1955, only a month before Einstein himself died.
sentences.zh: 爱因斯坦最好的朋友米凯莱·贝索于1955年去世，就在爱因斯坦本人去世前一个月。

sentences.en: Writing to Michaela's wife, he said,
sentences.zh: 他在写给米凯莱妻子的信中说，

sentences.en: What I admired most about Michaela was the fact that he was able to live so many years with one woman, not only in peace, but also in constant unity,
sentences.zh: 我最佩服米凯莱的是，他能够和一个女人生活这么多年，不仅相处融洽，而且始终保持着和谐，

sentences.en: something I have lamentably failed at twice.
sentences.zh: 而这一点我非常遗憾地失败了两次。

sentences.en: So in quitting this strange world, he has once again perceived me by little.
sentences.zh: 因此，在离开这个奇异的世界时，他又一次比我先走了一步。

sentences.en: That doesn't mean anything.
sentences.zh: 这其实并没有什么特殊的含义。

sentences.en: For those of us who believe in physics, this separation between past, present, and future is only an illusion, however tenacious.
sentences.zh: 对于我们这些相信物理学的人来说，过去、现在和未来之间的这种分离只是一种错觉，尽管它非常顽固。

sentences.en: So what he was saying there is that all these moments of your life actually exist, but you're just only experiencing one of them at a time.
sentences.zh: 所以他在那里表达的意思是，你生命中的所有时刻其实都同时存在，只是你一次只能体验其中一个。

sentences.en: It's kind of like the frames on a real film.
sentences.zh: 这有点像胶片电影里的画格。

sentences.en: You're watching a movie.
sentences.zh: 你在看一场电影。

sentences.en: The frames are all there, but you're only experiencing one at a time.
sentences.zh: 所有的画格都在那里，但你一次只能体验一个。

sentences.en: The rest are in the loop.
sentences.zh: 其余的都在循环中。

sentences.en: They've gone past, or they're still on the way.
sentences.zh: 它们已经过去，或者还在路上。

sentences.en: This is a sort of popular theory among physicists.
sentences.zh: 这是物理学家中一种很受欢迎的理论。

sentences.en: But I don't think there's any agreed upon theory or view of time.
sentences.zh: 但我认为并没有一个达成共识的关于时间的理论或观点。

sentences.en: If you go back far enough, then you run into the Big Bang, which is where everything began, as far as modern science knows.
sentences.zh: 如果你回溯得足够远，你就会遇到大爆炸，就现代科学所知，那是一切的起点。

sentences.en: We don't know where the universe came from, but we know that whatever made the universe also made space and time.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道宇宙从何而来，但我们知道，创造宇宙的万物也创造了空间和时间。

sentences.en: But the more physicists have looked at them, the more slippery they become.
sentences.zh: 但物理学家对它们研究得越多，它们就变得越捉摸不定。

sentences.en: And when you hold them up to the light, they start to fall apart.
sentences.zh: 当你在光线下审视它们时，它们便开始瓦解。

sentences.en: Because we're big creatures, we're made up of billions and billions and billions of atoMs.
sentences.zh: 因为我们是庞大的生物，由数不清的原子组成。

sentences.en: Our idea of time might be, if not wrong, only an approximation due to the fact that we're so big and last so long.
sentences.zh: 我们对时间的看法，即使不算错误，也只是一种近似，因为我们的体型如此庞大且存在的时间如此之长。

sentences.en: But reality could be like Chuck Close painting.
sentences.zh: 但现实可能就像查克·克洛斯的画作一样。

sentences.en: That when you look at it up close, there are all these little dabs and points of paint, and they don't seem to mean anything.
sentences.zh: 当你凑近看时，全都是一小点一小点的颜料，它们似乎没有任何意义。

sentences.en: It's only when you get on the other side of the room that they appear as fully formed portraits.
sentences.zh: 只有当你走到房间的另一端时，它们才会呈现出完整的肖像。

sentences.en: And in the same way, we kind of make sense of the world around us, because we're kind of seeing it averaged over many, many particles,
sentences.zh: 同理，我们之所以能理解周遭的世界，是因为我们看到的是无数粒子、

sentences.en: many, many very tiny, blindingly fast interactions and connections.
sentences.zh: 无数微小且快得耀眼的相互作用和连接被平均化之后的结果。

sentences.en: So where you are in the universe matters.
sentences.zh: 所以在宇宙中的位置是很重要的。

sentences.en: What conditions you're under in the universe matter.
sentences.zh: 你在宇宙中所处的条件也很重要。

sentences.en: Every place in the universe has kind of a different perspective.
sentences.zh: 宇宙中的每一个地方都有着某种不同的视角。

sentences.en: So Einstein had this great imagination.
sentences.zh: 所以爱因斯坦有着非凡的想象力。

sentences.en: He followed his thoughts.
sentences.zh: 他顺着自己的思路去思考。

sentences.en: And what he discovered is contrary to all our intuitions.
sentences.zh: 而他所发现的，与我们所有的直觉都相悖。

sentences.en: Meaning that time can speed up or slow down.
sentences.zh: 这意味着时间可以加速或减慢。

sentences.en: Things can shrink or expand depending on how they appear to be moving.
sentences.zh: 根据运动状态的不同，物体可以收缩或膨胀。

sentences.en: You know, matter can gather itself together and disappear into a black hole.
sentences.zh: 你知道，物质可以聚集在一起并消失在黑洞中。

sentences.en: I mean, these are crazy ideas.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这些都是疯狂的想法。

sentences.en: But there are now bedrock principles of the universe.
sentences.zh: 但它们现在已成为宇宙的基石原理。

sentences.en: He was the first one to show mathematically that the time just didn't work the way we thought it did.
sentences.zh: 他是第一个用数学方法证明时间并不像我们想象那样运作的人。

sentences.en: So he's undermined the whole idea, really, of kind of independent objective reality.
sentences.zh: 所以他实际上动摇了整个独立客观现实的概念。

sentences.en: If you look at the math, especially in relativity, it's just high school algebra.
sentences.zh: 如果你看看数学公式，尤其是相对论，那其实只是高中代数。

sentences.en: Anybody can do it.
sentences.zh: 任何人都能学会。

sentences.en: I mean, Einstein's secret was that he asked really good questions.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，爱因斯坦的秘诀在于他提出了非常好的问题。

sentences.en: If you have a question, you can answer it.
sentences.zh: 如果你有一个问题，你就能回答它。

sentences.en: But the real hard thing is coming up with a good question to begin with.
sentences.zh: 但真正困难的是一开始就能提出一个好问题。

sentences.en: I mean, part of the art craft of not just science, but I would even say, like novel writing,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，不仅是科学的一部分工艺，我甚至可以说，就像写小说一样，

sentences.en: is to ask a specific question that goes places you didn't dream.
sentences.zh: 关键在于提出一个能够带你走向意想不到之地的具体问题。

sentences.en: So how would you summarize the question that you think Einstein was setting out to answer?
sentences.zh: 那么，你觉得你会如何总结爱因斯坦着手解答的问题呢？

sentences.en: The question he set out to answer.
sentences.zh: 他着手去回答的问题。

sentences.en: He famously posed this to himself when he was 15 years old.
sentences.zh: 他在15岁时就向自己提出了这个著名的假设。

sentences.en: If he was traveling along a light beam at the speed of light, what would he see?
sentences.zh: 如果他以光速沿着光束旅行，他会看到什么？

sentences.en: That's the question?
sentences.zh: 就是这个问题吗？

sentences.en: That question unlocked 20th century physics.
sentences.zh: 这个问题开启了20世纪的物理学。

sentences.en: You would be surprised as anybody to find out that we can actually see these effects in the universe.
sentences.zh: 你会和任何人一样惊讶地发现，我们实际上可以在宇宙中观察到这些效应。

sentences.en: The space bending and warping.
sentences.zh: 空间在弯曲和扭曲。

sentences.en: We thought they were true.
sentences.zh: 我们以为它们是真的。

sentences.en: He just didn't think that it would be possible to actually observe them.
sentences.zh: 他只是没想到真的有可能观察到它们。

sentences.en: And they observed the bending of light around the sun during this eclipse in 1919.
sentences.zh: 他们在1919年的那次日食期间观察到了太阳周围光线的弯曲。

sentences.en: And that was what made him eternally famous.
sentences.zh: 正是这一点让他名垂青史。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好。

sentences.en: So going back to time, tell us about how we know which way time is moving.
sentences.zh: 那么回到时间的话题，给我们讲讲我们是如何知道时间流逝的方向的。

sentences.en: So our brains know which way time is going because of what they call entropy.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们的大脑之所以知道时间的走向，是因为所谓的熵。

sentences.en: What is entropy?
sentences.zh: 什么是熵？

sentences.en: Think of it as sort of a kind of the amount of disorder, messiness.
sentences.zh: 可以把它看作是一种无序度、混乱程度。

sentences.en: So it just means that in time, things get more disordered.
sentences.zh: 所以它只意味着随着时间的推移，事情会变得更加混乱。

sentences.en: Your closet gets messier.
sentences.zh: 你的衣橱变得更乱了。

sentences.en: Your desk gets messier.
sentences.zh: 你的办公桌变得更乱了。

sentences.en: And in general, entropy increases as you go through time.
sentences.zh: 总的来说，随着时间的推移，熵是在增加的。

sentences.en: So we get older and die.
sentences.zh: 所以我们会变老并死去。

sentences.en: We can't reverse entropy.
sentences.zh: 我们无法逆转熵。

sentences.en: So we're going to die.
sentences.zh: 所以我们终将一死。

sentences.en: So we're always stuck wasting energy.
sentences.zh: 因此我们总是不可避免地在浪费能量。

sentences.en: And it seems to be that that gives a direction to time.
sentences.zh: 这似乎赋予了时间一个方向。

sentences.en: We go from ordered states to more disordered states.
sentences.zh: 我们从有序的状态走向更加无序的状态。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: You know, a general colloquial way of saying it is that things get worse.
sentences.zh: 你知道，用通俗的话来讲，就是事情变得越来越糟。

sentences.en: And this is why I don't think we want to go into it like this.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我认为我们不应该这样深入探讨。

sentences.en: This is why you can't actually have a perpetual motion machine.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么你实际上无法拥有永动机。

sentences.en: Do not talk about perpetual motion machines.
sentences.zh: 不要谈论永动机。

sentences.en: This would be so confusing.
sentences.zh: 这会把人搞糊涂的。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 行吧。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So moving on to recap, time began with the Big Bang.
sentences.zh: 那么继续总结，时间始于大爆炸。

sentences.en: Then things became more and more disordered, which is how we know the direction that time is moving.
sentences.zh: 然后事情变得越来越无序，这就是我们如何知道时间流逝方向的原因。

sentences.en: What questions does this make you and scientists wonder about the end of time?
sentences.zh: 这让你和科学家们对时间的尽头产生了什么疑问？

sentences.en: I'm sorry.
sentences.zh: 抱歉。

sentences.en: Is that a cue for me or something?
sentences.zh: 这是给我的暗示什么的吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Well, if time had a beginning, can it also have an end?
sentences.zh: 好吧，如果时间有个开始，它也会有个终点吗？

sentences.en: What does that mean?
sentences.zh: 那是什么意思？

sentences.en: So if we look far enough ahead into the future, the stars will all have burned out.
sentences.zh: 所以如果我们向未来看够远，所有的恒星都将燃尽。

sentences.en: A lot of them will collapse into black holes.
sentences.zh: 它们中的许多会坍缩成黑洞。

sentences.en: The black holes will have evaporated and everything will be so far apart that they'll just be kind of these random particles wandering around.
sentences.zh: 黑洞会蒸发，一切都会相距如此遥远，以至于只剩下这些随机漫游的粒子。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So time is no longer moving directionally.
sentences.zh: 所以时间不再具有方向性地运动。

sentences.en: From order to disorder, it's just all disorder.
sentences.zh: 从有序到无序，现在全都是无序了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: There's no difference from one place to any other place.
sentences.zh: 任何一个地方和另一个地方都没有区别了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: That would be the end of time.
sentences.zh: 那将是时间的终结。

sentences.en: That's the best prediction astronomers can make right now.
sentences.zh: 这是天文学家目前能做出的最佳预测。

sentences.en: So that would just be it.
sentences.zh: 所以事情就会是这样。

sentences.en: The universe happened once.
sentences.zh: 宇宙只诞生过一次。

sentences.en: It was a great thing.
sentences.zh: 这是件了不起的事。

sentences.en: But for the vast length of its duration, there wouldn't be anything happening.
sentences.zh: 但在其漫长的生命周期里，大部分时间都不会有什么事情发生。

sentences.en: So this actually is the best time to be alive in the universe because there's a lot happening now.
sentences.zh: 所以现在其实是宇宙中最好的活着的时代，因为现在发生了很多事。

sentences.en: What's interesting to me is we kind of all create the same time.
sentences.zh: 对我而言有趣的是，我们某种程度上都在创造属于自己的时间。

sentences.en: Each one of us is in our own little bubble, right?
sentences.zh: 我们每个人都活在自己的小泡泡里，对吧？

sentences.en: Every one of us is the center of the universe because we all kind of see things from where we are.
sentences.zh: 我们每个人都是宇宙的中心，因为我们都是从自己所在的角度来看待事物。

sentences.en: So we all have a slightly different point of view.
sentences.zh: 所以我们每个人的观点都有所不同。

sentences.en: And amazingly, there's a lot we agree on.
sentences.zh: 而神奇的是，我们有许多共识。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: We share time and we also have our own sense of time.
sentences.zh: 我们共享时间，同时也拥有自己对时间的感知。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: So as Bob Dylan said, I'll let you be in my dream if I can be in yours.
sentences.zh: 正如鲍勃·迪伦所说，如果你让我进入你的梦，我就让你进入我的梦。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: That was great.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: Thanks for putting up with me, Dennis.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你包容我，丹尼斯。

sentences.en: Well, it's great for you to take this on.
sentences.zh: 哪里，你能接受这个挑战太棒了。

sentences.en: Talk to you soon.
sentences.zh: 回头聊。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Bye.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.en: Bye.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app unlocked.
sentences.zh: 纽约时报应用已解锁。

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 大家都知道，你需要订阅《时报》才能阅读所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month for free without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果你能免费体验《时报》一个月而无需输入信用卡呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你首次下载纽约时报应用时，你在应用中的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 有一个月的时间突破付费墙，看看时报订阅者每天都能获得什么。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是纽约时报的订阅者，今天就下载时报应用，获得30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天需要了解的其他消息。

sentences.en: It appears increasingly likely that the affidavit used to justify an FBI search of Donald Trump's home will be released.
sentences.zh: 用来证明搜查唐纳德·特朗普住所的联邦调查局搜查令宣誓书似乎很有可能会被公开发布。

sentences.en: On Thursday, a federal judge ordered that the Biden administration propose redactions to the affidavit to ensure that making it public would not disclose sensitive secrets.
sentences.zh: 周四，一名联邦法官下令拜登政府对宣誓书提出删节建议，以确保将其公之于众不会泄露敏感机密。

sentences.en: Affidavits for a search warrant are almost never released until charges are filed because they contain detailed information about a criminal investigation.
sentences.zh: 搜查令的宣誓书几乎从不在提起指控前公开，因为它们包含有关刑事调查的详细信息。

sentences.en: But media organizations have requested that this affidavit be made public now because it involves a former president.
sentences.zh: 但媒体机构已要求现在就公开这份宣誓书，因为它涉及一位前总统。

sentences.en: And Deshaun Watson, the star NFL quarterback,
sentences.zh: 而德肖恩·沃森，美国国家橄榄球联盟的明星四分卫，

sentences.en: has agreed to a tougher punishment than originally proposed over allegations that he repeatedly committed sexual misconduct during massage appointments.
sentences.zh: 已同意接受比最初提议更严厉的惩罚，此前有人指控他在按摩预约期间屡次实施性骚扰。

sentences.en: Watson, the subject of a recent daily episode, will be suspended for 11 games rather than just 6 games and pay a record $5 million in fines.
sentences.zh: 作为近期《每日新闻》节目的主题人物，沃森将被禁赛11场，而不是仅仅6场，并将支付创纪录的500万美元罚款。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Bianca Gaver with help from Corey Schreppel.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由比安卡·加弗制作，科里·施雷佩尔协助。

sentences.en: It was edited by Wendy Doerr with help from Anita Bonagio.
sentences.zh: 节目由温迪·多尔剪辑，安妮塔·博纳吉奥协助。

sentences.en: Our theme music is by Jim Rundberg and Ben Landverk of Wonderly.
sentences.zh: 我们的主题音乐由来自Wonderly的吉姆·伦德伯格和本·兰德维克创作。

sentences.en: Special thanks to Mae Ryan, who conceived of this project with Dennis.
sentences.zh: 特别感谢梅·瑞安，她与丹尼斯共同构思了这个项目。

sentences.en: Physicist Jana Levin, who consulted with Dennis on it.
sentences.zh: 物理学家雅娜·莱文，她就此项目咨询了丹尼斯。

sentences.en: And our audio department colleagues, Hans Butow, Tracy Mumford, Tali Abacassas, Anna Martin, and Tina Antolini.
sentences.zh: 还有我们的音频部门同事汉斯·布托、特蕾西·芒福德、塔利·阿巴卡萨斯、安娜·马丁和蒂娜·安托利尼。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是本期《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: See you on Monday.
sentences.zh: 周一见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个受严密控制的机器在运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 选举迎来了群自称改革派的人。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党便陷入了一场残酷、混乱且有时令人兴奋的权力斗争中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro, with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在最新一期的《都市》节目中，我，萨拉·科尼格，将讲述人们试图维持其影响力却在过程中失去控制的故事。

sentences.en: Metro.
sentences.zh: 《都市》。

sentences.en: Listen wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 在你获取播客的任何地方收听。

sentences.en: We'll see you next time.
sentences.zh: 我们下期再见。
